amount.note: The report is due by the entity's expiration date, the last day of the month in which it was formed. The first one falls a year after formation.

notIncluded.label: Initial report
notIncluded.reason: Free when filed with the Certificate of Formation, which is how the estimate assumes it is filed. Filed separately within the first months, it costs a small fee.

sources.title: Washington Secretary of State - LLC and PLLC filing resource page

notIncluded.label: Late annual report fee
notIncluded.reason: Only if the annual report is filed after the expiration date.

sources.title: Washington Secretary of State - LLC and PLLC filing resource page

notIncluded.label: Registered agent service
notIncluded.reason: Only if you hire a registered agent. The agent sets the price, so it is not a state fee and is not in the total.

notIncluded.label: Name reservation
notIncluded.reason: Optional. Reserving a name before you file is a separate charge and is not in the total.

notIncluded.label: Expedited filing and certified copies
notIncluded.reason: Optional. Faster processing and certified copies cost extra and are not in the total.

notIncluded.label: Local business licenses and permits
notIncluded.reason: City, county and industry licenses depend on where the business operates and what it does. None are in the total.

notIncluded.label: Federal and state income taxes
notIncluded.reason: Taxes on the LLC's or its owners' income are not part of this estimate. This page is not legal or tax advice.

content.intro: {state} charges a one-time fee to file a Certificate of Formation and an annual report fee each year after that.

howItWorks.text: The Secretary of State lists the same Certificate of Formation fee for online and paper filing.
The initial report is free when filed with the Certificate of Formation. Filed later, within the first months, it has a small fee.
The annual report is due by the last day of the month in which the LLC was formed. A late report adds a delinquency fee.

faq.q: Do I need to file an initial report in {state}?
faq.text: Yes. It is free if you file it with the Certificate of Formation, and costs a small fee if filed separately.
